tldr: Most headlines frame the story as a political crisis: Zelensky 'bowing to pressure' after an 'unpopular military purge,' with Ukrainian and regional outlets counting protest days and demanding Fedorov's return. A secondary track across Western and Asian factual outlets treats the story as a personnel announcement — profiling new commander Drapatyi — while Russian state media alone frames the appointment as proof of a war prolonged at terrible human cost.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline using dehumanizing propaganda framing: 'Ukraine has a new butcher-in-chief – all the better to feed Ukrainians to the grinder' frames the appointment as continuity of a losing, costly war — absent from every other outlet including independent Russian press.

'Ukraine's Cardboard Maidan Shows That the People Still Matter' is the only headline that labels the protest phenomenon and draws a Maidan parallel, framing popular pressure as democratic wartime accountability rather than political disruption.
The only outlet using day-count headlines ('Day Nine,' 'Eighth Day') to frame the protests as a sustained, escalating timeline — reinforcing the sense of an unresolved, ongoing political standoff.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, Ukraine's military shake-up reads primarily as a political accountability crisis — Zelensky bowing to protest pressure after an 'unpopular purge' — while most factual and international outlets quietly profile the incoming commander, and Russian state media alone frames the reshuffle as proof of a war prolonged at terrible human cost.
